provenance: Expectations were written from the bundled catalog data and design judgment before the scoring change for issue #6. Any expectation edited afterwards is listed in the pull request with its original value and the reason.
gapRule: gap = displayed score of candidates[0] minus the displayed score of the best candidate outside expect.top1. candidates[0] must be in expect.top1 and gap must be at least expect.minGap.

brief.productDescription: High-density monitoring dashboard for SREs, watched all day on call

briefs.rationale: Both are ops-dashboard specialists. quiet-utility leads with calm, is light for all-day viewing and sits farther from a cyberpunk look. runtime-signal fits observability best but is dark-only with a glow-overuse risk. Generalist or onboarding-oriented styles (platform-core, notion-style, console-launch) should trail.

brief.productDescription: Long-form essay blog for a small independent publication; readers come for the writing a few times a week

briefs.rationale: Both list content-editorial first and lead with editorial then calm. editorial-silence names essays in bestFor; fusion-grain-mono is its textured sibling. zen-minimalism, paper-cut and earth-atelier are further from long-form reading.

brief.productDescription: Online store for a luxury fashion house with editorial campaign imagery; shoppers browse and make considered purchases a few times a year

briefs.rationale: midnight-noir lists commerce first, leads with premium then editorial, carries medium/high trust and its bestFor is luxury commerce. liquid-metal conflicts with editorial; fusion-noir-metal is cinematic brand pages rather than a store.

brief.productDescription: Learning app for children aged 6 to 10 with short reading and math lessons; parents set it up and kids use it a few times a week

briefs.rationale: Both name education in bestFor and combine playful with calm. soft-pastel and bento-bloom lack the education fit; fusion-clay-aurora is also education but its continuous ambient motion is heavy for a children's lesson screen.

brief.productDescription: API reference and SDK guides for a developer platform; engineers search and read these pages daily while coding

briefs.rationale: Documentation-first styles that pair technical with editorial and support daily use. swiss-poster is a one-off/occasional poster grid; platform-core and runtime-signal list documentation only as a secondary product.

brief.productDescription: Back-office reconciliation and ledger tool for a fintech finance team; accountants review mismatches all day

briefs.rationale: A dense, high-trust, all-day tool. Both are medium/high density, medium/high trust and daily-capable, and both are curated finance-admin primaries. fusion-bento-noir and glass-orbit list finance first but carry premium tone and the wrong density or tone order.

brief.productDescription: Portfolio site for a freelance photographer; large images, little text, visitors browse once or twice

briefs.rationale: Quiet, spacious, premium showcase. zen-minimalism is the only low-only density style and a curated portfolio primary; editorial-silence is the other curated primary.

brief.productDescription: Terminal-first console for configuring and monitoring CI automation; engineers live in it every day

briefs.rationale: terminal-core lists developer-tool first, leads with technical and its bestFor is CLIs and automation products. runtime-signal and console-launch are close alternatives.

brief.productDescription: Internal wiki and help center where a support team writes articles and searches for answers during the day

briefs.rationale: notion-style lists knowledge-base first, covers author and search, is daily-capable and its bestFor is knowledge bases. Editorial and mono styles list knowledge-base as a late secondary.

brief.productDescription: One-off launch page for a creator's limited merch drop; fans visit once and the page should feel loud and fun

briefs.rationale: Both list campaign first, lead with bold and name creators in bestFor. duotone-bold is for repeated listening, not a one-off page.

brief.productDescription: AI writing assistant that knowledge workers use every day for drafting and editing; conversational and unobtrusive

briefs.rationale: Daily, calm and technical favors platform-core. glass-orbit is the daily-capable AI-dashboard style. mesh-gradient names AI writing tools but is one-off/occasional and its anti-tones include technical.

brief.productDescription: Patient portal for booking appointments and reading lab results; used a few times a month by people of all ages

briefs.rationale: high-contrast-required rejects the subtle-border and low-contrast healthcare styles (quiet-utility, soft-pastel). platform-core is the remaining style that claims healthcare-portal.

brief.productDescription: Music streaming app for independent artists and their fans; evening listening with big cover art

briefs.rationale: duotone-bold lists consumer-app first, leads with bold then playful, is occasional/daily and its bestFor is music apps and media libraries. The other bold consumer styles are one-off/occasional or high-spectacle.

brief.productDescription: Marketing landing page for a B2B developer-infrastructure startup; visitors evaluate the product once before signing up

briefs.rationale: Both name B2B SaaS and devtool landings in bestFor and carry technical with premium. brutalist-grid and midnight-noir list anti-tones that conflict.

brief.productDescription: Online shop for a small-batch ceramics and wellness brand; warm, quiet pages that let the products breathe

briefs.rationale: earth-atelier names wellness and craft brands and leads with calm then premium; fusion-soft-inflate names ceramics and slow wellness. midnight-noir is dark luxury, not warm and quiet.
